title: Index Funds vs Active Mutual Funds
content: An index fund passively tracks a market benchmark (like the S&P 500) with ultra-low expense ratios (often 0.03%-0.10%). Actively managed funds employ managers who attempt to outperform the market, charging higher expense ratios (0.50%-1.50%). Over a 15-year horizon, over 85% of active managers underperform index funds due to fees and turnover drag.

title: Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA)
content: Dollar-cost averaging is the strategy of investing a fixed dollar amount at regular intervals regardless of asset price. This removes emotional market-timing risk and ensures you buy more shares when prices are low and fewer when prices are high, lowering average purchase cost over time.
